headlines.title: Tokenized stocks face pushback as NYSE, Nasdaq pivot for a new market
headlines.summary: OKXICE is set to debut Monday despite objections from 90% of the companies whose stocks it initially proposed to list.
headlines.article_text: Tokenized stocks face pushback as NYSE, Nasdaq pivot for a new market Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points People involved in talks with some of the companies say a 30-day objection window left them little time to react and decide if they were ready to participate. In this article ICE Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Traders work on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York City, Nov. 10, 2026. Angela Weiss | AFP | Getty Images OKXICE, a trading platform for tokenized securities jointly operated by Intercontinental Exchange and crypto exchange OKX, is set to debut Monday despite objections from 90% of the companies whose stocks it initially proposed to list. Of the 62 companies whose shares OKXICE first sought to trade, 56 objected to having their shares tokenized and traded on the platform, according to a review of public notices posted between Oct. 4 and Nov. 5 . By last week, even more companies had objected , including those not on the original roster. The high objection rate may reflect companies' lack of readiness to have blockchain-based representations of their shares traded on a new third-party platform like OKXICE, rather than broad resistance to tokenization. People involved in talks with some of the companies say a 30-day objection window left them little time to react and decide if they were ready to participate. `Revolutionary,' 'transformational' "The shift to a 24/7 global marketplace is revolutionary and transformational for our market structure," Andrew Cuomo, co-chair of OKXICE, told CNBC. "The majority of companies aren't familiar with [tokenization] and haven't had a chance to understand it and the consequences." "Logic dictates that many companies were going to be cautious before they understood what the system would do," added Cuomo, who served 10 years as governor of New York until 2021. "What you're seeing now is the more the companies learn about 24/7 global access, the more receptive they are." At launch, tokenized shares of Coinbase , Robinhood , Strategy , Circle , Securitize and BitGo will be available to trade on the platform, OKXICE disclosed in a public notice. OKXICE has confirmed 113 assets, including exchange-traded funds and products, going live on a rolling basis. Since its initial pre-launch announcement on Nov. 11, OKXICE said it's seen further interest from different issuers and Fidelity Investments , Direxion, eToro , Strive and Vida Global are now participating. The 30-day opt-out window is a requirement of the SEC's so-called Innovation Exemption , which took effect in September and temporarily permits the trading of certain tokenized stocks. Under the exemption, trading platforms must notify the underlying issuers and give them an opportunity to object. Any issuer who objects blocks its shares from being tokenized. "We've gotten a lot of feedback that the reason why you've seen this high number of rejections of tokenizing equity is because it was a 30-day window," Seth Ginns, chief investment officer at Franklin Templeton's crypto arm, told CNBC at the Digital Assets Forum in New York earlier this month. Many issuers were open to exploring the idea but were hesitant to move forward amid competing priorities, he said. "[They're] saying it's earnings season, there was the midterms, there's a lot going on during this 30-day window. Give us some time, we want to learn about it, we're not closed to the idea we're just closed to rushing into it right now," Ginns added. Announcement timing Ran Grushkowsky, CEO of MassPay, a global payout platform, said several of his company's clients were among the initial targets and shared that their concern was less about the concept of tokenization and more about how 24/7 trading could affect stock value and investor relations strategies, particularly around the timing of corporate announcements. "It's more [about] what's going to be the effect, how is it going to actually drive the value of the stock," he said. "A lot of the strategy that happens around investors relations has to do with scheduling and when you announce certain things and so how do you do it when your stock is being traded 24/7?" watch now VIDEO 9:59 09:59 Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo on scaling tokenization and expanding beyond digital securities Crypto "The executives were actually quite excited about this new innovation and potentially getting more interest into the stock. It was really from the [investor relations] side that they received push back," and heard "let's hold off," Grushkowsky added. The lack of awareness may even extend to executives overseeing digital asset initiatives, suggesting that some rejections stem from internal communication gaps and unfamiliarity with the process, according to Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo, whose company is one of the first being listed on OKX. Securitize is also the tokenization partner for OKX. "We've talked to some of the issuers that have opted out [where] the head of digital assets doesn't even know who in the company rejected them," he said. "This is a consequence of, first, the novelty of the process and of these venues, and second, the lack of understanding of what they're being notified to do." watch now VIDEO 3:05 03:05 Robinhood CEO on tokenization: It allows us to distribute access to U.S. stocks globally Squawk Box Despite the initial pushback, Domingo expects more issuers to participate as companies become more familiar with the model, noting that some regulated trading venues can operate without issuer consent. Long game Company objections raise a separate question about which of the different tokenization models will prove most attractive. The main alternative to the OKXICE model is an issuer-led approach that integrates blockchain-based shares into existing regulated market infrastructures, with issuers retaining greater control over the process. Bullish, a digital asset platform, is pursuing an example of this model through its partnership with Equiniti, the transfer-agent business it's acquiring for $4 billion . Nasdaq's planned launch of an issuer-centric tokenized equities model in partnership with Kraken parent Payward in the second quarter of next year could offer a test of that framework and whether companies are more willing to embrace tokenization under a different structure. Nasdaq and the New York Stock Exchange, owned by Intercontinental, and others are responding to a structural shift in how securities are issued, traded and settled. Tokenization has become attractive to institutions and investors because it enables round the clock stock trading, shortened settlement times, fractional ownership and eases the use of securities as collateral. watch now VIDEO 11:31 11:31 How big banks like JPMorgan and Citi want to put Wall Street on a blockchain Crypto World For the exchanges, it presents a way to keep control of trading and market infrastructure as crypto-native, blockchain-based venues seek to bring traditional financial assets on to blockchain. It's a long way off before it becomes a meaningful revenue driver, however, according to Clear Street analyst Owen Lau. "It increases the [total addressable market], that's the number one thing," Lau said. "In the near term, there may not be enough of an incremental revenue opportunity, but the trend is there. The company's board wants the next leader to have an expertise in software and self-driving technology, Bloomberg said, citing people familiar with the board's thinking. Anderson came to GM in June 2025, leaving behind the self-driving vehicle technology startup he co-founded, Aurora Innovation. Prior to that he was the director of autopilot programs at Tesla. — Michelle Fox 56 Min Ago Dollar General rises on upgrade Shares of Dollar General moved 2% higher on the back of an upgrade to overweight from neutral at Piper Sandler. Plus, the company's steady growth profile is appealing in an increasingly volatile market environment, he said. — Michelle Fox 1 Hour Ago LuxExperience pops after JPMorgan upgrade JPMorgan upgraded the luxury digital retailer to overweight from neutral on Monday, sending U.S.-listed shares up 6.6% in premarket trading. "We believe recent weakness in the banks provides us the opportunity to buy TFC, as new CEO Mike Lyons will make incremental progress improving the returns and EPS power over time. We expect Lyons and his team to improve the economics of its balance sheet while self-funding growth initiatives to jump-start revenue growth longer term." — Fred Imbert 2 Hours Ago Nvidia, Anthropic surge in early trading Shares of Nvidia and Anthropic popped 8% and 4%, respectively, as investors scooped up AI-linked names at a discount after a steep sell-off last week . headlines.article_text: SpaceX sued by 2 states over AI deepfake porn, Grok safety claims Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Virginia and Oregon are the first states to sue Elon Musk's SpaceX, alleging it harmed consumers and falsely marketed its Grok AI image generator as generally safe. Grok, which is integrated with social network X, has enabled users to generate and share explicit deepfakes based on real images of children and women who did not consent, research shows. The states' attorneys general are seeking civil penalties, fees and to make SpaceX put stricter guardrails in place. In this article SPCX Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Jonathan Raa | Nurphoto | Getty Images Lawsuits against Elon Musk's SpaceX are stacking up, with Virginia and Oregon becoming the first states to sue the company over issues with its Grok AI image generator. Versions of Grok and SpaceX's social network X have enabled users to generate and distribute explicit deepfakes based on real photos or videos of children and other people who did not consent, according to research by the Internet Watch Foundation , the Center for Countering Digital Hate and others. In separate complaints submitted to state courts as of Monday morning, Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield and Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones argued that SpaceX failed to put safeguards in place to stop Grok and X users from making and sharing harmful deepfake images, especially alleged AI-generated child sexual abuse material. The complaints also allege that SpaceX has falsely represented its AI apps and social network (Grok and X) as generally safe, which the states see as a violation of Virginia's Consumer Protection Act or Oregon's Unlawful Trade Practices Act. The matter is particularly concerning because X allows minors 13 and older to access its content. Rayfield and Jones both noted in their complaints that harms caused by non-consensual, sexualized images go beyond the victims depicted in the images. "This content can cause fear, distress, and anxiety in those who are unwillingly exposed to the content," Jones wrote. Rayfield wrote that such conduct "erodes important norms regarding consent and privacy and trivializes sexual imagery, abuse, and exploitation." SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment. At an NYC Council hearing in October , a SpaceX AI policy leader, Gabriela Castillo Madrid, said the company had appropriate "safeguards" and "strict controls" in place around its AI products. SpaceX was already facing multiple Grok- and X-related lawsuits, and government probes around the world, including by authorities in the U.K., Spain, Ireland, France and the state of California. In private-sector lawsuits filed against SpaceX in the U.S. concerning Grok and AI-generated, explicit images, litigation is still in early stages and is tracked by The Center for Internet Technology Addiction. When the city of Baltimore sued xAI, now owned and operated by SpaceX, the company argued that under Section 230, they were not liable for unwanted images. Section 230 is a federal law that largely shields online platforms from liability for users' content. SpaceX also sued a user in a federal court in the Northern District of Texas for breach of contract after he allegedly used Grok to create and distribute deepfake explicit images, including depictions of minors. Lawyers for Musk's company argued that Grok should be seen as "a neutral tool, subject to user control," and that any image generation "is the result of the user's prompts and directions." The new state suits add to legal pressure on SpaceX. Both Virginia and Oregon are seeking injunctions, civil penalties, disgorgement and legal costs, while Virginia is also seeking restitution for consumers from Musk's company. Oregon submitted its complaint to the Multnomah County Circuit Court on Sunday evening, and Virginia submitted its complaint to the City of Richmond Circuit Court Monday morning . As of early Monday, the suits were pending the courts' acceptance. State attorneys general have recently succeeded in compelling U.S. social media companies to change their products and pay for alleged past harms. In August, for example, Meta settled a major federal case centered on allegations that the social media giant misrepresented the level of child mental health problems caused by its apps, Facebook and Instagram . Without admitting to wrongdoing, Meta agreed to pay states around $17 billion over a 10-year period and to make app changes that experts believe will help keep children safer online.
